summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on experience building and debugging robot runtime software across firmware, perception, and control layers. Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic arm system coordinating a camera, sensors, and a Jetson+Arduino controller into one real-time runtime, and derived full forward-kinematic chains for 6-DoF and 5-DoF arms validated against MoveIt/RViz. Comfortable moving between Python, C/C++, bare-metal STM32 firmware, and PCB bring-up to debug hardware and software issues end to end.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design in SolidWorks and CAD, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented UART/I2C sensor communication with closed-loop feedback control.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation in a laboratory research environment.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition device (ADXL345 + Raspberry Pi + Bluetooth) translating hand motion into HID commands via Python; resolved sensor jitter through hardware/software debugging and calibration.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system as a coordinated robot runtime spanning a mobile client, edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller over one WebSocket fabric.

Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2x speedup, 56.7->10.9 ms) for visual servoing and ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping; resolved 11 integration failures for 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ driving five servos with range-gated contact detection; deployed the runtime as a systemd service for reliable multi-device operation.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and forward-kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt/RViz in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e via the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability <2mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Applied autonomy and perception pipelines (YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson) to track objects, driving an STM32 over UART with PWM servo controls, FreeRTOS task coordination, and ToF distance sensing.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon - National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
